markdown_chunks.section: **Performance Analysis and Mass Estimation of a Small-Sized Liquid** **Rocket Engine with Electric-Pump Cycle** > 123
markdown_chunks.text:
**4 Conclusion**

In this paper, the applicability of the electric-pump cycle was
reviewed through performance analysis of the 500 N thrust
as a small-sized liquid rocket engine. The actual commercial
motor and battery were applied to the performance analysis and mass estimation. The simulation results showed that
the motor and battery mass were heavier than the minimum

values of commercial products. In addition, the application
of the compact system was possible using the present technology maturity in the power unit. The electric-pump cycle
showed a heavier mass compared to the driving element
(power), but propellant was saved by the absence of a gas
generator, thereby reducing the overall mass of the tank, feed
line, and shortening the components, resulting in a lighter
total mass. As a result, the mass in the power components,
which was analyzed as a disadvantage of the electric-pump
cycle, was compensated, and the dry mass showed lighter
results than the gas generator cycle. Finally, the engine performance factors of the electric-pump cycle, such as specific
impulse and speed increment, were superior. In conclusion,
the electric-pump cycle has a mass advantage over the gas
generator cycle in a small-sized liquid rocket engine, highlighting the possibility of mounting a commercial motor and
battery. On the other hand, the final applicability and performance of the electric-pump cycle as a small-sized rocket
engine should be evaluated more realistically through further
studies, including the dynamic characteristics of the propellant supply system, including the power unit.
